## 8eeb98656c43

**The ordinary generator cannot distinguish the selected color-specific rule
from a color-blind shortcut.** It emits only red (`2`) objects on the left,
while the selected rule mirrors only red cells and paints their reflections
orange (`7`). A learner can therefore infer “mirror every nonzero left-half
cell” and fit every generated example.

Concrete counterexample accepted by `self_check`: an 8×11 grid with
`(0,0)=2`, `(1,1)=8`, and all other cells zero. `self_check` returns `[]`.
The selected rule adds orange only at `(0,10)` and leaves the blue cell
unmirrored. The color-blind shortcut additionally adds orange at `(1,9)`.
A lawful mixed-color left-half witness (or a stricter validator if such inputs
are intentionally unlawful) is needed to prevent this shortcut.
